text: Preserve or refuse on unmodeled top-level keys in checkpoint disposition rewrites. core.AbandonCheckpoint (internal/core/checkpoint_disposition.go) and events.ResolveCheckpoint perform the same parse -> mutate -> re-marshal round-trip on a pre-existing file, so unmodeled TOP-LEVEL keys are still dropped on abandon and resolve even after 146-F / 129-S lands. U2 fixes the nested `context` loss as a side effect; the top level needs either a raw top-level carrier or an explicit refusal-to-mutate policy, which is a distinct design decision from the create boundary. Residual exposure: all nine live files under .backlogit/checkpoints/ carry such keys. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 1 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md (Scope boundaries and recorded follow-ups); parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S; external source 3C7AAC71. NOT release-blocking for 129-S.

Classify syncWriteFileAtomic outcomes by converging internal/events onto the existing internal/atomicfile leaf - which already tags ErrWriteNotApplied and ErrWriteIndeterminate - rather than adding a second classifier inside the private duplicate, then surface indeterminate checkpoint creates with path and context keys on both transports. Today events.CreateCheckpoint writes through syncWriteFileAtomic (internal/events/fsutil.go) with no outcome classification and no injectable seam, and neither the MCP errorResponse nor the CLI error path can carry a path or a key list, so a create whose write is indeterminate returns a bare error and the caller cannot tell "probably written" from "not written". Needs a classified write result, a handler-level seam, and a new error envelope on both surfaces. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 2 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md; parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S. Descoped from 129-S because it is traceable to neither external source 3C7AAC71 nor 90F2A9F8. NOT release-blocking for 129-S.

Drop omitempty from MigrateReport collection fields. MigrateReport.Applied and MigrateReport.Skipped (internal/docline/report.go) carry omitempty and therefore vanish entirely on a zero-apply run - a known adjacent instance of the always-an-array contract that 146-F / 129-S fixes only for LintReport.Findings and the new checkpoint context_keys. Residual exposure: a zero-apply migrate report omits both arrays, so an agent cannot distinguish "nothing applied" from "field absent". Compound reference: docs/compound/2026-07-21-omitempty-defeats-arrays-always-json-contract.md. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 3 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md; parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S; external source 90F2A9F8. NOT release-blocking for 129-S.

Converge LintTree and PlanMigration on the one classifyDecodeFailure helper. After 146-F / 129-S lands, docline.LintTree reports-and-continues on a per-file frontmatter decode failure while docline.PlanMigration still aborts the whole corpus on the first one - two decode policies over one frontmatter grammar inside the same package. PlanMigration is read-only, so the write-path safety rationale that justifies ApplyMigration's all-or-nothing abort does not apply to it. U8 introduces the unexported classifyDecodeFailure(err) (rule string, fatal error) helper in internal/docline/service.go with a containment/decode/read-failure/nil table test as its convergence lock; this follow-up adopts that same helper in PlanMigration so a second decode policy is never written. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 4 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md, and named as the recorded convergence follow-up in plan unit U8; parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S; external source 90F2A9F8. NOT release-blocking for 129-S: the divergence is introduced by 129-S and is recorded as accepted residual exposure.

Decide whether create_checkpoint becomes a governed operation. 146-F / 129-S deliberately does NOT add a governed: true marker or a governed_name for create_checkpoint in .autoharness/backlog-registry.yaml, because the governed-parity design requires a named behavioral fixture per marker and that is a separate decision. Neither the registry nor the MCP-to-CLI fallback guide describes a create_checkpoint result shape or flag semantics affected by U6, so 129-S introduces no registry drift. Residual exposure: create_checkpoint stays ungoverned, with CLI/MCP parity enforced only by U5a's cross-surface harness rather than by the registry drift test. Needs deliberation before implementation. References: docs/design-docs/governed-operation-parity.md, docs/compound/2026-08-15-governed-parity-fixtures-must-dispatch-authoritative-registry.md. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 5 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md; parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S. NOT release-blocking for 129-S.

Upstream the checkpoint context Continuity Protocol wording into backlogit.instructions.md.tmpl. Plan unit U10b edits .github/instructions/backlogit.instructions.md in this repository so agents learn that for a schema_version: 1 dump the arbitrary recovery keys belong INSIDE context, that the top level and progress are closed, that a rejected create means "retry with the keys nested under context" rather than "session state is lost", and that checkpoint context is unredacted git-tracked durable state that must not carry secrets. That file is autoharness-generated from backlogit.instructions.md.tmpl, which lives in a repository 146-F / 129-S treats as strictly read-only under Principle IV / PA-5, so the in-repo edit is silently reverted by the next autoharness regeneration. This follow-up upstreams the same wording into the template. The durable, non-generated statement of the contract remains U4b's backlogit_create_checkpoint MCP tool description. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 6 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md, referenced from plan unit U10b's Generated-artifact caveat and acceptance; parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S; external source 3C7AAC71. NOT release-blocking for 129-S: it is executed in the upstream harness repository, not in this one, so it cannot be a member of 129-S.

Provide a structured JSON error envelope for CLI validation failures mirroring the MCP shape. After 146-F / 129-S lands, MCP carries a structured unknown_fields []string array on an unknown-key checkpoint rejection (plan unit U4b) while the CLI prints a wrapped error string, so an agent driving the CLI must read message text to learn which keys were rejected while an agent driving MCP gets a parseable list. Adding a JSON error-serialization path to the CLI is a general output-contract change affecting every CLI error, not just this one, and is untraceable to either in-scope external source. Compound reference: docs/compound/2026-07-03-cli-mcp-honest-fallback-map-and-registry-drift-test.md. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 7 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md; parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S. NOT release-blocking for 129-S.

Decide the gitignore and redaction posture for checkpoint context. .backlogit/checkpoints/ is NOT gitignored and its files are tracked. 146-F / 129-S opens the checkpoint context namespace, which makes it materially easier for an agent to persist arbitrary unredacted session state to a git-tracked path; changing the tracking posture mid-shipment would rewrite unrelated repository conventions, so 129-S deliberately leaves it unchanged and mitigates only with U10b's documented secrets caveat. Residual exposure: unredacted agent-supplied context continues to be committed to git, and Principle XI forbids history rewriting so git revert cannot purge a committed blob. Needs deliberation covering gitignore posture, redaction at the write boundary, and whether a size or key allowlist is warranted. Provenance: scope-boundary follow-up 8 of 8 recorded in docs/exec-plans/2026-08-21-success-shaped-evidence-loss-plan.md, and cross-referenced from the plan's Decisions table row on unredacted durable state and its Plan Hardening Signals security row; parent work feature 146-F, shipment 129-S; external source 3C7AAC71. NOT release-blocking for 129-S.

Review follow-up (129-S / 146-F): no MCP tool equivalent of `backlogit docs classify <path>` exists (backlogit_docs_lint/migrate/scope are all present, but classify is CLI-only). Consider adding a `backlogit_docs_classify` MCP tool wrapping docline.Classify for CLI/MCP parity. Raised by Agent-Native Parity Reviewer during 129-S structured review; pre-existing gap, not introduced by this shipment.

Review follow-up (129-S / 146-F): The CLI's `checkpoint create` closed-schema-namespace rejection only exposes a plain-text error (via fmt.Errorf wrapping *CheckpointUnknownFieldError), while the MCP surface returns a structured {error, message, unknown_fields} response. Consider factoring a shared, transport-agnostic response builder from *CheckpointUnknownFieldError so the CLI (and its --jsonrpc mode) can expose unknown_fields structurally too, and/or add an optional `data` field to internal/cli/format.JSONRPCError per JSON-RPC 2.0 so structured domain errors (unknown_fields, mutation-partial classification, checkpoint disposition codes, etc.) don't degrade to a string on the CLI's JSON-RPC surface. Raised by Agent-Native Parity Reviewer during 129-S structured review; explicitly out of scope for 146.012-T (task text scoped this to MCP only).

Review follow-up (129-S / 146-F, harness hygiene): commit-message.instructions.md documents a closed commit-scope vocabulary (mcp, cli, db, core, models, telemetry, config, docs, tests, ci, harness) and a 300-byte body limit, but repo-wide practice (including this shipment's own commits) regularly uses additional scopes (events, docline, memory, compound, cli-reference) and longer bodies for larger multi-bullet commits. Raised by Constitution Reviewer during 129-S structured review. Consider either updating commit-message.instructions.md's scope enumeration/body-length guidance to match actual practice, or tightening future commits to the documented limits — this is a pre-existing, repo-wide drift, not specific to this shipment.

Review follow-up (129-S / 146-F, PR #373, deferred at review-fix cycle limit): CheckpointContext.Extra is an exported field and can be constructed directly (bypassing UnmarshalJSON's guarantee that every stored json.RawMessage came from a real decode). CheckpointContext.emit() (used by both MarshalJSON and Keys()) appends each Extra value verbatim without validating it is well-formed JSON, so a directly-constructed CheckpointContext with a nil or malformed json.RawMessage in Extra makes MarshalJSON() return invalid JSON bytes with a NIL error, and Keys() likewise reports success despite the same emit() result being unserializable. Fix: validate each Extra raw value (e.g. json.Valid(v)) in emit() before appending, and return an error naming the offending key if invalid. Add a regression test constructing a CheckpointContext directly with a malformed Extra value and asserting MarshalJSON/Keys() both return an error rather than silently producing broken JSON. Deferred past the 3-cycle review-fix limit (circuit-breaker.instructions.md).

Shipment 129-S ship-time gate blocked: backlogit_ship_shipment refuses to archive shipment 129-S (feature 146-F, PR #373, merged as 15ab30a2) because task 146.006-T's recorded pre_task_completion_gate_passed evidence head_sha (52f1983516a65ef2d782f75d137426ae5a63dc21) is not an ancestor of the merged main HEAD -- the commit is a dangling/orphaned object (not reachable from any branch), almost certainly due to a history rewrite (rebase/amend) during the long PR #373 review-fix cycle. Verified the underlying code change IS present at current main HEAD (internal/events/checkpoint_schema.go carries CheckpointContext.UnmarshalJSON/MarshalJSON/Keys() exactly as that commit introduced them), so this is a benign stale-evidence artifact, not missing work or a security incident. All other 22 manifest members (146-F plus 146.001/002/004/005/007-024-T) pass the lineage ancestry check cleanly against the same HEAD. No supported, non-destructive repair tool exists in the current backlogit surface: UnarchiveItem (internal/core/archive.go) is not exposed via any CLI command or MCP tool, and CLI `move --force-gates` is documented as inapplicable to items in the terminal `archived` status ("archived is a terminal sink with no allowed status transitions, so it cannot be force-gated" -- internal/core/shipment_gate.go). Recommend one of: (a) add a supported CLI/MCP operation to re-run or force a member's ship-time gate-evidence check for an already-archived task against the current shipment head with an explicit operator-approved justification, mirroring the existing --force-gates contract; or (b) add an explicit, audited exemption path for a single dangling-evidence commit when the identical file/functions are independently verifiable at the shipment head. Until resolved, shipment 129-S remains status=active (not shipped) and feature 146-F remains logically complete (status=done, archived) but the release is not formally closed for P-001 purposes. See docs/closure/2026-08-22-146-f-129-s-closure.md for full detail and docs/memory/2026-08-22/ship-129-s-post-merge-closure-memory.md for the reconciliation evidence.
